SK3503 An IAsyncDisposable is disposed synchronously

A plain using on a type that offers DisposeAsync, inside a body where await using would compile.

CategoryLifetime
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, review it
Language version floorC# 8.0
Since1.2

Why

A type implements IAsyncDisposable because its cleanup does something that has to be waited for — a final flush, a graceful close, a return to a pool. Its synchronous Dispose therefore either blocks the thread on that work or skips it, and both are decided by the type rather than by the caller. Taking the asynchronous path is how the caller stops depending on which one this type chose.

Example

Instead of:

async Task WriteAsync(Stream target) {
    using (var writer = new StreamWriter(target)) {
        await writer.WriteLineAsync("done");
    }
}

Write:

async Task WriteAsync(Stream target) {
    await using (var writer = new StreamWriter(target)) {
        await writer.WriteLineAsync("done");
    }
}

The ReSharper mapping

⚠ The export sets resharper_use_await_using_highlighting = suggestion and this rule defaults to warning. ReSharper treats it as a style preference; doc 08 puts the id in the disposal-and-lifetime band, where the default is warning, and doc 00's ninth non-negotiable says a severity comes from what the rule means rather than from how loud it is. Reading the ReSharper key (off by default, doc 03 § "Severities") would demote it to suggestion.

When it does not fire

⚠ Only where `await using` compiles, which is a narrower place than where the pattern is wrong. The nearest enclosing method, local function or lambda must already be async, and the using must not sit in a position where await is illegal — a lock body, a constructor, an operator, an initializer, a query clause, an unsafe block, an expression tree. A using in a synchronous method is not reported at all, because making that method async changes its signature and is a refactor rather than an edit. ⚠ The disposed type must implement System.IAsyncDisposable as resolved by the semantic model, never be guessed from a DisposeAsync member of the right name. ⚠ What the rule cannot know is whether this particular type's `Dispose` is a complete implementation, and for several BCL types it is; those findings are correct and are not necessarily worth acting on, which is what a baseline entry is for rather than a reason to lower the severity. The fix inserts one keyword and is marked unsafe because await using introduces a suspension point where there was none, and a suspension changes when the code after it runs.
